title: Orders sell well below list price and discounts stack on top
evidence: Order value is 9,390,803 against 11,080,268 at list price.
65% of orders are priced below list (price is 75-100% of list), costing 916,044.
discount_pct adds a further 773,421 on top.
Largest gap by category: Home (324,657).
action: Review who can set prices below list and cap stacked discounts (price cut + discount_pct).
assumptions: list_price is treated as the reference price. Order prices track list price (correlation 0.99) at 75%-100% of list, so this is a systematic markdown, not noise.

title: A large share of orders are sold below unit cost
evidence: 38% of all orders sell below unit cost; completed orders with negative profit lose 1,214,116.
94 of 250 products have negative total profit; 76 have unit cost above list price.
Lowest category margin: Beauty at 7.1% (others up to 35.2%).
action: Check cost and price master data first, then reprice or stop selling the worst products.
assumptions: README says costs and prices were generated independently, so margins may be unrealistic. Treat as a data-quality and pricing alert, not proven loss.

title: Cancelled orders (9.4% of orders): no reliable driver found
confidence: No driver detected in this data
evidence: 1689 orders, value 861,850.
9 segment tests run; 1 passed p<0.05 before correction, 0 after Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
Most extreme gap: quantity=4 at 10.2% vs 9.4% overall (adjusted p=0.20).
Model A test AUC 0.524 (95% CI [0.493, 0.554]): NO RELIABLE SIGNAL: AUC interval includes 0.50 (random). Do not use for decisions.
Permutation test (100 shuffles): real AUC 0.524 vs shuffled 0.5 +/- 0.019, p=0.139. NOT distinguishable from random labels.
action: Do not target specific segments. Reduce cancelled with process fixes (checkout, delivery, product information) and track the rate monthly.
assumptions: Synthetic data: absence of a driver here does not prove none exists in real data.

model.verdict: NO RELIABLE SIGNAL: AUC interval includes 0.50 (random). Do not use for decisions.

title: Pending orders stuck for months
evidence: 918 orders are Pending, worth 466,933.
824 of them are older than 30 days (median age 180 days), worth 417,527.
Pending share by month: chi-square p=0.14 (no month stands out, so not just recent orders).
action: Run a weekly pending-order sweep: confirm, cancel or escalate anything older than 30 days.
assumptions: Age measured at the last data date (2025-12-31).

title: Campaign spend with extreme cost per conversion and impossible funnels
evidence: 171 of 1200 campaigns report impossible funnels (clicks>impressions or conversions>clicks); spend on them is 674,503.
Isolation Forest flagged 180 campaigns; their spend above median efficiency (median cost per conversion 5.26) is 197,854.
Model B caught 104 of 171 impossible-funnel rows (recall 61%).
Correlation between spend and conversions is -0.005 (Spearman p=0.89): extra spend is not associated with more conversions.
action: Pause or audit flagged campaigns and fix tracking so clicks and conversions are recorded correctly.
assumptions: Excess spend assumes the median cost per conversion is achievable. Campaign conversions (895,411) cannot be reconciled with 18,000 orders.

model.note: Sanity check only: impossible-funnel rows (clicks>impressions or conversions>clicks) are a rule-based proxy, not ground truth.

title: Products likely to stock out before the supplier delivers
verdict: REAL (computed from stock, sales velocity, lead time)
evidence: 8 of 250 products have fewer days of cover than supplier lead time plus average delay; 26 more are below reorder point.
Estimated revenue at risk: 8,026 (shortfall days x average daily completed revenue per product).
stockout_flag is NOT related to stock level, supplier delay or reorder point (p=0.27, 0.72, 0.78), so it is ignored in this analysis.
action: Reorder the listed products now, starting with the largest shortfall, and confirm how stockout_flag is defined.
assumptions: Sales velocity is the average over the whole year from non-cancelled orders; inventory is not linked to sales, so lost sales are an estimate.
